advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that sets `tracker.branch` to a non-default value (e.g. 'ledger') and asserts upstream_branch_refs excludes `refs/remotes/origin/ledger` while INCLUDING a code branch named `refs/remotes/origin/tickets`.
evidence: Commit message: 'resolved through config.tickets_branch() so a renamed event-log branch stays excluded'
tests/unit/test_commit_impact.py:50: `local = _clone_with_remote_branches(tmp_path, "main", ["main", "tickets"])` — the only exclusion test uses the literal default name 'tickets'
search of tests/ for `_excluded_upstream_branch` returns (no matches); no test sets tracker.branch and checks exclusion via upstream_branch_refs

Named violating input: a repo with `tracker.branch = "ledger"` and remote branches `origin/ledger` (event log) + `origin/main` (code) — a broken resolver would walk `origin/ledger` (wrong history) and, if the exclusion stayed hardcoded, would wrongly drop a code branch named `origin/tickets`; no test detects either regression.
advisory.finding: The new unit suite never exercises the config-driven exclusion: it only excludes the hardcoded default branch name 'tickets', so the diff's headline behavior — resolving the excluded branch through rebar.config.tickets_branch(repo_root) so a RENAMED event-log branch stays excluded — has no regression coverage. Replacing the tickets_branch(repo_root) call with the constant "tickets" would leave every test green.
scenarios: A future refactor hardcodes the exclusion to "tickets" or breaks the config wiring; the renamed-branch layout regresses undetected.
A repo that renames tracker.branch away from 'tickets' and happens to also have a code branch literally named 'tickets'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test building a clone whose upstream has both an event-log branch matching a configured `tracker.branch = "ledger"` and a code branch `tickets`, with a `[tool.rebar]` config on the local repo, asserting `refs/remotes/origin/ledger` is absent and `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` and `refs/remotes/origin/main` are present.
